title: Regent
name: Lattimer
description: The Regent is a decisive, pragmatic statesman who seized the opportunity of a lifetime and has held on to it well. He wants the Kingdom well run, and is better at running it than many born to the task, because he knows when to be kind and when to be brutal, and how to justify either. He means well, but meaning well takes power, and he can no longer always tell whether his jostling for influence is for his people or for himself.
history: The Regent was born to a middling family of the Capital and rose as high as such a birth allows, to alderman of the ward around the University. When the University's great library burned, he organised the bucket lines, spoke to the crowd on its steps and had the wing rebuilt within the year, and when no cause for the fire could be found, he made sure a culprit was. He was not grand enough to be invited to the feast at which the royal court was killed, and so survived it. That night he was the one who stood up and calmed the Capital, and the cantrev lords made him Regent, expecting an alderman to be easily managed.
summary: A shrewd and eloquent Regent, an alderman raised by a massacre, who governs the Kingdom well and is learning to love the game of power.

appearance.features: Full greying beard, heavy brows, deep-set eyes

clothing.head: Flat velvet cap
clothing.body: Heavy dark robe with a broad collar
clothing.accessories: The alderman's chain of office, which he still wears

notes: Speaks in two registers: warm, plain and rousing before a crowd, dry and clipped in private, where every conversation is a transaction
Always knows what a crowd needs to hear, and says it. He invents nothing, but lends his voice to any rumour that suits him, such as the Uncrowned Order's guilt
Works long hours, reads every report himself and knows each of his clerks by name
Quietly resents the nobles who look down on his birth, and takes particular pleasure in outmanoeuvring them
